issue_context.title: ApiServer: Inconsistent behaviors for MergePatch and JsonPatch with invalid patchBytes
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

This issue is revealed in #97200.

When patchBytes cannot be Unmarshaled for both MergePatch and JsonPatch, these two types will return different error types. MergePatch will return the unmarshal error "Invalid JSON Patch" and JsonPatch will return converted badRequest error.

**What you expected to happen**:

Both MergePatch and JsonPatch should return badRequest when invalid patchBytes provided.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Currently this issue is hided by the sanity checks reverted in #97215. Once we remove the sanity checks and send a large patch(cannot be Unmarshaled successfully) in both MergePatch and JsonPatch type, they will return "Invalid JSON Patch" and badrequest errors.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:

- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

/cc @liggitt 
/assign

review_comments: this change unmarshals all merge patches twice... the previous code only did so for ones over 1MB... I'd prefer not to regress patch performance as part of removing this workaround.

What I want to achieve here is that when users sent patchBytes fail to be unmarshalled for MergePatchType, api-server will return a bad request error same as for JSONPatchType, not simply remove the sanity check.

The previous failing tests try to send bytes over 1MB and check whether get a bad request error which is returned by the sanity check. But for bytes below 1MB, even they cannot be unmarshalled successfully, it will return `fmt.Errorf("Invalid JSON Patch")` instead of bad request. Removing the sanity check will make bytes over 1MB return `fmt.Errorf("Invalid JSON Patch")` because they cannot be unmarshalled successfully as well.

For performance issue, does it make sense to make `jsonpatch.errBadJSONPatch` public and then we can check it here to avoid duplicated unmarshal? 

https://github.com/evanphx/json-patch/blob/147e2b447e4274fdaacdf8d02e08e87933d3120e/merge.go#L92

> For performance issue, does it make sense to make jsonpatch.errBadJSONPatch public and then we can check it here to avoid duplicated unmarshal?

Some way of understanding whether the error came from the doc, the patch, or the application of the patch to the doc would make sense to me, so we could return a BadRequest if the patch itself was bad.
